I’ll be honest: my homebrew iPhone lens mod does look a bit ridiculous — but it actually makes iPhone photography more practical and a lot more fun.

What started as a solution to a one-off shooting problem has become something I instinctively reach for…

One of the biggest divides in the compact camera world is whether you need a viewfinder. Back in the day, old-school camera fans would argue endlessly about electronic viewfinders (EVFs) versus optical ones, but EVFs are now so good that hardly anyone cares anymore.

Whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder has real advantages over using the rear screen for composing shots — especially in harsh sunlight. Even cranked up to maximum brightness, it’s still hard to see the display clearly in strong sun, and the screen is prone to reflections.

In London this has never really been a major issue, but this summer we’ve been hit by record-breaking heatwaves, and honestly it feels like the last time I saw a cloud or any rain was about thirty years ago.

But for me, there’s more to it than that. I’ve noticed a difference in visual engagement between using a viewfinder and using the rear screen — with a viewfinder you only see the frame, whereas with the rear screen you take in the whole surroundings. Sometimes it’s exactly that sense of immersion that makes me reach for a dedicated camera rather than my iPhone.

When I was choosing a camera for video a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was the clear standout, but the lack of a viewfinder put me off. In the end I decided it wasn’t a deal-breaker, since I’d mainly be using it indoors, and even when shooting outside, attaching a big monitor with a sun hood would solve most of the problems.

But sometimes I want something more streamlined to operate, rather than a full rig with a monitor bolted on, so I found a simple accessory that’s perfect for outdoor use. It’s essentially a sun hood combined with a magnifying lens that magnetically attaches to the camera’s rear screen, giving you something akin to an optical viewfinder.

I had a shoot recently where I needed to use the BMPCC 4K alongside my iPhone 16 Pro Max. I went to the location for a quick test, and that viewfinder accessory was a huge help. Since the BMPCC 4K and the iPhone have similarly sized screens, I wondered whether the same accessory might also work with my iPhone.

Obviously the iPhone doesn’t have a magnetic array, but the phone is light enough that simply holding it up against the magnifying lens works perfectly. The effect blew me away — especially being able to use the Camera Control button as a shutter release.

I’ve since used the accessory to shoot in all sorts of situations, and being able to see the screen clearly in bright sun, as well as that immersive feel, has made the whole process far more enjoyable. My iPhone has long been my primary camera, and with this homebrew mod I find I’ll reach for just the phone in more situations.

Genius or madness? Let me know what you think in the comments. If you’re on the genius side, I’m afraid the specific model I bought seems to have been discontinued, and I’ve never come across anything similar designed for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, drop the link in the comments.
